description: This module covers the core concepts, services, and best practices for building generative AI solutions on AWS. It includes foundation models, Amazon Bedrock and its features (Knowledge Bases, Agents, Guardrails), Amazon Q products, LLM architecture fundamentals, generative AI application patterns, embeddings, vector databases, and no-code tools like PartyRock. Mastery of these topics is essential for the AWS AI Practitioner certification.

topics.definition: Foundation models are large-scale machine learning models pre-trained on broad, diverse datasets that can be adapted (fine-tuned or prompt-engineered) to a wide range of downstream tasks. They exhibit emergent capabilities such as reasoning, summarization, and code generation. Examples include Claude (Anthropic), Titan (Amazon), Llama (Meta), and GPT (OpenAI). FMs are typically trained using self-supervised learning on massive corpora of text, images, or code, and their generality distinguishes them from task-specific models.

Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed AWS service that provides access to high-performing foundation models from leading AI companies (Anthropic, Meta, Stability AI, Cohere, Mistral, Amazon) through a single, unified API. It allows developers to build and scale generative AI applications without managing infrastructure. Key capabilities include model selection, fine-tuning, Retrieval Augmented Generation via Knowledge Bases, autonomous task execution via Agents, content safety via Guardrails, model evaluation, and provisioned throughput for production workloads. All data remains private and is not used to train the underlying models.

topics.topicName: Amazon Bedrock APIs (InvokeModel and Converse API)
topics.definition: Amazon Bedrock exposes APIs for interacting with foundation models. The InvokeModel API sends a prompt to a specified model and returns a response, supporting both synchronous and streaming (InvokeModelWithResponseStream) modes. Each model has its own request/response schema. The Converse API provides a model-agnostic, unified interface for multi-turn conversations, abstracting away model-specific prompt formatting differences. It supports tool use (function calling), system prompts, conversation history management, and makes it simple to switch between models without rewriting application code.

Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases implement Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), a pattern that enhances foundation model responses with information retrieved from an organization's private data sources. The service automatically ingests documents from Amazon S3, chunks them, generates vector embeddings, and stores them in a supported vector database (Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Pinecone, or Redis Enterprise Cloud). At query time, the user question is embedded, semantically similar chunks are retrieved, and the retrieved context is injected into the prompt sent to the FM, reducing hallucinations and grounding answers in authoritative data.

Amazon Bedrock Agents enable foundation models to autonomously execute multi-step tasks by orchestrating calls to APIs, data sources, and knowledge bases. Developers define action groups (backed by AWS Lambda functions or OpenAPI schemas) that the agent can invoke. The agent uses chain-of-thought reasoning to decompose a user request, determine which actions to take, call the appropriate APIs, and synthesize a final response. This makes it possible to build AI assistants that can look up order status, make reservations, query databases, or trigger business workflows without manual intervention.

Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provide configurable safeguards that sit between the user and the foundation model to enforce responsible AI policies. Guardrails can filter harmful content across categories (hate speech, violence, sexual content, misconduct), block denied topics to keep conversations on-topic, redact or mask personally identifiable information (PII), filter hallucinated responses using automated reasoning checks, and manage inappropriate word lists. Guardrails can be applied to any model on Bedrock and operate on both inputs (prompts) and outputs (responses).

topics.topicName: Amazon Q (Q Business and Q Developer)
topics.definition: Amazon Q is a family of generative AI-powered assistants. Amazon Q Business is an enterprise assistant that connects to corporate data sources (S3, SharePoint, Salesforce, Confluence, Slack, etc.) via connectors, enabling employees to ask questions, get summaries, and create content grounded in organizational knowledge, with access controls respecting existing permissions. Amazon Q Developer is an AI coding companion (formerly CodeWhisperer) that provides real-time code suggestions, code transformation (e.g., Java 8 to Java 17), vulnerability scanning, chat-based debugging, and can operate within IDEs and the AWS Management Console to help with AWS resource management.

Large Language Models are built on the Transformer architecture, which uses self-attention mechanisms to weigh the relevance of every token in a sequence relative to every other token, enabling the model to capture long-range dependencies. Tokenization converts raw text into numerical token IDs that the model processes; common schemes include Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) and SentencePiece. Key architectural elements include multi-head attention, positional encoding (or embeddings), feedforward layers, and layer normalization. Parameters such as temperature, top-p (nucleus sampling), and top-k control the randomness and creativity of the generated output.

Common generative AI application patterns include: text generation (drafting emails, articles), summarization (condensing long documents), code generation (writing and explaining code), image generation (creating images from text prompts via diffusion models), question answering (extracting answers from context), chatbots (multi-turn conversational agents), classification (sentiment analysis, intent detection), and translation. Effective application design involves prompt engineering, choosing the right model size and modality, managing context windows, implementing RAG for grounding, and applying guardrails for safety.

Embeddings are dense numerical vector representations of data (text, images, or other content) that capture semantic meaning in a high-dimensional space. Semantically similar items have vectors that are close together, enabling similarity search. Vector databases (such as Amazon OpenSearch Serverless with vector engine, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, and Redis Enterprise Cloud) are purpose-built to store, index, and query these embedding vectors efficiently using approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) algorithms. Embeddings are foundational to RAG pipelines, recommendation systems, and semantic search.

Amazon Titan is Amazon's family of foundation models available on Bedrock. Titan Text models (Titan Text Express, Titan Text Lite, Titan Text Premier) handle text generation, summarization, and classification tasks. Titan Embeddings models (Titan Embeddings G1, Titan Multimodal Embeddings) convert text or text-and-image inputs into vector representations for search and RAG. Titan Image Generator creates and edits images from text or image prompts, supporting inpainting, outpainting, and image variation. All Titan models include built-in watermarking to promote responsible AI use.

PartyRock is an Amazon Bedrock-powered, no-code platform that allows anyone to build, share, and explore generative AI applications through an intuitive drag-and-drop interface in a web browser. Users create apps by describing them in natural language and combining widgets (text generation, chatbot, image generation). PartyRock requires no AWS account or coding experience, making it an accessible playground for learning about prompt engineering, generative AI concepts, and rapid prototyping of AI-powered app ideas.

questions.question: A company wants to build a generative AI application using multiple foundation models without managing any infrastructure. They need the flexibility to switch between models from different providers. Which AWS service should they use?

options.A: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
options.B: Amazon Bedrock
options.C: Amazon Comprehend
options.D: Amazon Lex

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that provides access to foundation models from multiple providers (Anthropic, Meta, Amazon, Cohere, Mistral, Stability AI) through a single unified API. It requires no infrastructure management and supports easy model switching. SageMaker JumpStart also offers FMs but requires more infrastructure management. Comprehend is for NLP analytics, and Lex is for building conversational bots, not general-purpose FM access.

questions.question: What is a foundation model (FM)?

options.A: A small, task-specific model trained on a narrow dataset for a single use case
options.B: A large-scale model pre-trained on broad, diverse data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks
options.C: A rule-based system that uses if-then logic to generate responses
options.D: A model that can only be used for natural language processing tasks

questions.explanation: Foundation models are large-scale machine learning models pre-trained on broad, diverse datasets using self-supervised learning. Their key characteristic is generality: they can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks through fine-tuning or prompt engineering. They are not limited to NLP (multimodal FMs handle images, code, etc.), and they are the opposite of small, task-specific models.

questions.question: Which Amazon Bedrock API provides a model-agnostic interface for multi-turn conversations, eliminating the need to format prompts differently for each model?

options.A: InvokeModel API
options.B: ListFoundationModels API
options.C: Converse API
options.D: CreateModelCustomizationJob API

questions.explanation: The Converse API provides a unified, model-agnostic interface for multi-turn conversations on Amazon Bedrock. It abstracts away the model-specific prompt formatting differences, supports conversation history, tool use, and system prompts. InvokeModel requires model-specific request formats. ListFoundationModels lists available models, and CreateModelCustomizationJob is for fine-tuning.

questions.question: A healthcare company wants to use a generative AI model but needs to ensure that personally identifiable information (PII) in patient queries is masked before reaching the model. Which Amazon Bedrock feature should they use?

options.A: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
options.B: Amazon Bedrock Agents
options.C: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
options.D: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails can be configured to detect and redact or mask PII in both inputs (prompts) and outputs (responses). This ensures sensitive patient information is not sent to the foundation model. Knowledge Bases are for RAG, Agents are for task orchestration, and Model Evaluation is for comparing model performance.

questions.question: In the Transformer architecture used by LLMs, what is the primary purpose of the self-attention mechanism?

options.A: To compress the input text into a smaller representation for storage
options.B: To allow each token to weigh the relevance of every other token in the sequence
options.C: To convert text into numerical token IDs
options.D: To apply grammatical rules to the generated output

questions.explanation: Self-attention allows the model to compute a weighted representation of each token by considering its relationship to every other token in the sequence. This enables the model to capture long-range dependencies and contextual meaning. Tokenization (option C) converts text to token IDs but is a separate preprocessing step, not part of the attention mechanism.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a foundation model provider available on Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: Anthropic (Claude)
options.B: OpenAI (GPT)
options.C: Meta (Llama)
options.D: Stability AI (Stable Diffusion)

questions.explanation: OpenAI models (GPT-3.5, GPT-4) are not available on Amazon Bedrock. Bedrock provides access to models from Anthropic (Claude), Meta (Llama), Stability AI (Stable Diffusion), Amazon (Titan), Cohere (Command), Mistral (Mistral, Mixtral), and AI21 Labs (Jamba). OpenAI models are available through Azure OpenAI Service or OpenAI's own API.

questions.question: A company wants their generative AI application to answer questions using information from internal company documents stored in Amazon S3. The answers must be grounded in actual company data to minimize hallucinations. What should they implement?

options.A: Fine-tune a foundation model on the company documents
options.B: Use Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases to implement RAG
options.C: Increase the model's temperature parameter
options.D: Use a larger context window model and paste all documents into the prompt

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases implement Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), which automatically ingests documents from S3, creates vector embeddings, and retrieves relevant context at query time to ground the model's responses in actual company data. This reduces hallucinations. Fine-tuning teaches style/format but doesn't reliably inject factual knowledge. Increasing temperature increases randomness. Pasting all documents is impractical and exceeds context limits.

questions.question: What is the purpose of embeddings in the context of generative AI?

options.A: To encrypt data before sending it to a foundation model
options.B: To convert data into dense numerical vector representations that capture semantic meaning
options.C: To compress large files for faster network transfer
options.D: To split large documents into smaller pages for printing

questions.explanation: Embeddings are dense numerical vector representations that capture the semantic meaning of data (text, images, etc.) in a high-dimensional space. Semantically similar items have vectors that are close together, enabling similarity search, clustering, and retrieval. They are foundational to RAG, recommendation systems, and semantic search. They do not relate to encryption or file compression.

questions.question: An enterprise wants to build an AI assistant that can look up order statuses from their order management API, query a product knowledge base, and book return shipments, all in a single conversational interaction. Which Amazon Bedrock feature is best suited for this?

options.A: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
options.B: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
options.C: Amazon Bedrock Agents
options.D: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Agents can autonomously orchestrate multi-step tasks by calling APIs (via Lambda functions or OpenAPI schemas), querying knowledge bases, and chaining actions together using chain-of-thought reasoning. This is exactly what's needed for an assistant that must look up orders, query a knowledge base, and trigger return shipments. Knowledge Bases alone only handle retrieval, and Guardrails handle content safety.

questions.question: Which Amazon Titan model is specifically designed to convert text into vector representations for use in semantic search and RAG pipelines?

options.A: Titan Text Express
options.B: Titan Image Generator
options.C: Titan Embeddings
options.D: Titan Text Premier

questions.explanation: Amazon Titan Embeddings (Titan Embeddings G1 and Titan Multimodal Embeddings) is specifically designed to convert text (or text and images) into dense vector representations for use in semantic search, RAG pipelines, and similarity matching. Titan Text models are for text generation, and Titan Image Generator is for image creation.

questions.question: What is PartyRock?

options.A: An AWS service for training custom foundation models from scratch
options.B: A no-code, Amazon Bedrock-powered platform for building and sharing generative AI apps in a web browser
options.C: An AWS database service optimized for storing vector embeddings
options.D: A command-line tool for deploying machine learning models on Amazon EC2

questions.explanation: PartyRock is an Amazon Bedrock-powered, no-code platform that allows anyone to build, share, and explore generative AI applications through a drag-and-drop web interface. It requires no AWS account or coding experience and is designed as an accessible playground for learning about prompt engineering and generative AI concepts.

questions.question: In the context of LLMs, what does the temperature parameter control?

options.A: The maximum number of tokens the model can generate
options.B: The speed at which the model processes the input
options.C: The randomness and creativity of the model's output
options.D: The number of attention heads in the transformer

questions.explanation: Temperature controls the randomness of the model's output distribution. A lower temperature (e.g., 0) makes the model more deterministic and focused, selecting the most probable tokens. A higher temperature increases randomness and creativity by flattening the probability distribution. It does not affect processing speed, token limits, or model architecture.

questions.question: A developer is using the Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel API and wants to display the model's response to the user as it is being generated, token by token, rather than waiting for the complete response. Which approach should they use?

options.A: Set the temperature to 0 for faster response
options.B: Use the InvokeModelWithResponseStream API
options.C: Use the ListFoundationModels API with a callback
options.D: Enable provisioned throughput on the model

questions.explanation: The InvokeModelWithResponseStream API enables streaming responses, allowing the application to display tokens as they are generated rather than waiting for the entire response. This improves perceived latency and user experience. Setting temperature to 0 affects output determinism, not delivery speed. Provisioned throughput increases capacity but does not enable streaming.

questions.question: Which of the following vector databases is supported by Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases for storing embeddings?

options.A: Amazon DynamoDB
options.B: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
options.C: Amazon Redshift
options.D: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (with vector engine), Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (with pgvector), Pinecone, and Redis Enterprise Cloud as vector stores. DynamoDB is a key-value/document database, Redshift is a data warehouse, and ElastiCache for Memcached is an in-memory cache, none of which are supported vector stores for Bedrock Knowledge Bases.

questions.question: Amazon Q Developer provides which of the following capabilities?

options.A: Building ETL pipelines for data lakes
options.B: Real-time code suggestions, code transformation, and vulnerability scanning within an IDE
options.C: Managing Amazon EC2 instance fleets
options.D: Creating vector embeddings from source code files

questions.explanation: Amazon Q Developer (formerly Amazon CodeWhisperer) is an AI coding companion that provides real-time code suggestions, code transformation (e.g., upgrading Java versions), vulnerability scanning, chat-based debugging, and assistance with AWS services directly within IDEs and the AWS Console. It is not an ETL, fleet management, or embedding tool.

questions.question: What is Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)?

options.A: A technique for training models on augmented images to improve generation quality
options.B: A pattern that retrieves relevant information from external data sources and includes it in the prompt to ground the model's response
options.C: A method for compressing model parameters to reduce inference latency
options.D: A process of generating synthetic training data to augment existing datasets

questions.explanation: RAG is a pattern that enhances foundation model responses by first retrieving relevant information from external knowledge sources (such as documents, databases, or APIs) and then including that context in the prompt. This grounds the model's response in factual, up-to-date information, reducing hallucinations. It is not about image augmentation, model compression, or synthetic data generation.

questions.question: A company wants to prevent their customer service chatbot from discussing topics unrelated to their products, such as politics or competitors. Which Amazon Bedrock Guardrails capability should they configure?

options.A: PII redaction filters
options.B: Denied topic filters
options.C: Word filters
options.D: Content category filters

questions.explanation: Denied topic filters in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails allow you to define specific topics that the model should not engage with. By configuring denied topics for politics, competitors, etc., the chatbot will refuse to discuss those subjects and stay on-topic. PII redaction handles personal information, word filters block specific words, and content category filters handle harmful content categories.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes tokenization in the context of LLMs?

options.A: The process of encrypting text for secure transmission
options.B: The process of converting raw text into numerical token IDs that the model can process
options.C: The process of splitting a document into individual sentences
options.D: The process of assigning security tokens to API requests

questions.explanation: Tokenization in LLMs is the process of breaking raw text into sub-word units (tokens) and converting them into numerical IDs that the model can process. Common tokenization schemes include Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) and SentencePiece. Tokens may represent whole words, sub-words, or individual characters depending on the scheme. This is unrelated to encryption or security tokens.

questions.question: A startup with no AWS account wants to quickly prototype a generative AI chatbot app without writing any code. Which tool should they use?

options.A: Amazon SageMaker Studio
options.B: PartyRock
options.C: Amazon Bedrock Console
options.D: AWS Cloud9

questions.explanation: PartyRock is a no-code platform powered by Amazon Bedrock that does not require an AWS account. Users can build generative AI applications (including chatbots) through a drag-and-drop web interface by describing their app in natural language. SageMaker Studio, the Bedrock Console, and Cloud9 all require an AWS account and varying levels of technical expertise.

questions.question: In Amazon Bedrock, what is the purpose of provisioned throughput?

options.A: To enable fine-tuning of foundation models
options.B: To guarantee a reserved level of model inference capacity for production workloads
options.C: To store documents for RAG in a vector database
options.D: To enable multi-region deployment of models

questions.explanation: Provisioned throughput in Amazon Bedrock allows customers to purchase a reserved level of inference capacity (measured in model units) for a specific foundation model. This guarantees consistent performance and throughput for production workloads, independent of on-demand traffic patterns. It does not relate to fine-tuning, RAG storage, or multi-region deployment.

questions.question: Which Amazon Titan model includes a built-in watermarking capability to help identify AI-generated content?

options.A: Only Titan Text models
options.B: Only Titan Image Generator
options.C: All Titan models include built-in watermarking
options.D: Titan models do not support watermarking

questions.explanation: All Amazon Titan models include built-in watermarking as part of Amazon's responsible AI commitment. For Titan Image Generator, this means invisible watermarks are embedded in generated images. For Titan Text models, watermarking is applied to generated text outputs. This promotes transparency and responsible use of AI-generated content.

questions.question: A developer wants to use the same application code to switch between Claude and Llama models on Amazon Bedrock for multi-turn chat. Which API should they use to minimize code changes?

options.A: InvokeModel API with model-specific formatting
options.B: Converse API
options.C: CreateModelCustomizationJob API
options.D: GetFoundationModel API

questions.explanation: The Converse API provides a model-agnostic interface for multi-turn conversations. It uses a unified request and response format regardless of the underlying model, so developers can switch between Claude, Llama, and other models without changing their application code. InvokeModel requires model-specific prompt formatting, making it harder to switch models.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of RAG over fine-tuning when a company needs a model to answer questions about frequently updated internal documents?

options.A: RAG is always cheaper than fine-tuning
options.B: RAG retrieves current information at query time, while fine-tuning requires retraining to incorporate new data
options.C: RAG produces more creative responses than fine-tuning
options.D: RAG does not require any foundation model

questions.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant information from external data sources at query time, meaning the knowledge base can be updated without retraining the model. Fine-tuning bakes knowledge into model weights during training, requiring retraining whenever the source data changes. For frequently updated documents, RAG is far more practical. RAG still requires a foundation model to generate the final answer.

questions.question: In the RAG pipeline used by Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, what happens to documents during the ingestion phase?

options.A: Documents are sent directly to the foundation model for memorization
options.B: Documents are chunked, converted to vector embeddings, and stored in a vector database
options.C: Documents are translated into multiple languages for broader access
options.D: Documents are compiled into a fine-tuning dataset

questions.explanation: During ingestion, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases automatically splits documents into chunks, generates vector embeddings for each chunk using an embedding model (such as Titan Embeddings), and stores the embeddings in a configured vector database. At query time, the user's question is also embedded and used to retrieve semantically similar chunks. Documents are not sent to the FM for memorization or used for fine-tuning.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of Amazon Bedrock regarding data privacy?

options.A: Customer data is used to improve the base foundation models
options.B: Customer data and prompts are not used to train or improve the base foundation models
options.C: Data is shared across AWS accounts for collaborative model improvement
options.D: All data must be encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock ensures that customer inputs (prompts) and outputs (responses) are not used to train or improve the base foundation models. Customer data remains private and is not shared with model providers or other customers. While encryption with KMS keys is supported, it is not mandatory for all data.

questions.question: A company wants to use a generative AI model to create product images from text descriptions. Which model on Amazon Bedrock is best suited for this task?

options.A: Anthropic Claude
options.B: Cohere Command
options.C: Stability AI Stable Diffusion or Amazon Titan Image Generator
options.D: Meta Llama

questions.explanation: For text-to-image generation, Stability AI's Stable Diffusion models and Amazon Titan Image Generator are the appropriate choices on Amazon Bedrock. Both can generate images from text prompts. Claude, Command, and Llama are text-based language models that do not generate images.

questions.question: What is the role of action groups in Amazon Bedrock Agents?

options.A: They define the topics the agent is not allowed to discuss
options.B: They specify the APIs and Lambda functions the agent can invoke to complete tasks
options.C: They configure the vector database for knowledge retrieval
options.D: They set up content moderation filters for the agent's responses

questions.explanation: Action groups in Amazon Bedrock Agents define the set of APIs and AWS Lambda functions that the agent can call to perform tasks. Each action group is backed by either a Lambda function or an OpenAPI schema that describes the available operations, their parameters, and return values. The agent uses these action groups to execute multi-step tasks autonomously.

questions.question: Amazon Q Business connects to corporate data sources using which mechanism?

options.A: Direct database queries via JDBC
options.B: Pre-built data source connectors (e.g., for S3, SharePoint, Confluence, Salesforce)
options.C: Manual CSV file uploads only
options.D: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams

questions.explanation: Amazon Q Business uses pre-built data source connectors to integrate with corporate data sources such as Amazon S3, Microsoft SharePoint, Atlassian Confluence, Salesforce, Slack, and many others. These connectors handle authentication, crawling, and indexing of enterprise data. It does not require manual CSV uploads or JDBC connections.

questions.question: What is top-p (nucleus) sampling in the context of text generation with LLMs?

options.A: A method that selects the top p percent of training data for fine-tuning
options.B: A decoding strategy that samples from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds the threshold p
options.C: A technique for pruning p percent of model parameters to reduce model size
options.D: A metric that measures the top p percent accuracy of the model

questions.explanation: Top-p (nucleus) sampling is a decoding strategy where the model considers the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability mass exceeds the specified threshold p (e.g., 0.9). This dynamically adjusts the number of candidate tokens based on the probability distribution, allowing more diversity when the model is uncertain and more focus when it is confident.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a supported use case for Amazon Titan Image Generator?

options.A: Text-to-image generation
options.B: Image inpainting (editing parts of an image)
options.C: Real-time video generation from text
options.D: Image outpainting (extending an image beyond its borders)

questions.explanation: Amazon Titan Image Generator supports text-to-image generation, image inpainting (modifying specific areas of an existing image), outpainting (extending an image beyond its original borders), and image variation (creating similar images). It does not support real-time video generation, which is a different and significantly more complex capability.

questions.question: A data scientist needs to compare the performance of different foundation models on Amazon Bedrock for a specific use case before deploying to production. Which Bedrock feature should they use?

options.A: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
options.B: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation
options.C: Amazon Bedrock Agents
options.D: Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation allows users to evaluate and compare the performance of different foundation models using automatic evaluation metrics (accuracy, robustness, toxicity) or human evaluation. This helps data scientists select the best model for their specific use case before production deployment.

questions.question: In the context of Amazon Bedrock, what does fine-tuning a foundation model accomplish?

options.A: It increases the model's context window size
options.B: It adapts the model's weights using domain-specific or task-specific training data to improve performance on particular tasks
options.C: It reduces the model's inference cost by compressing parameters
options.D: It enables the model to access real-time internet data

questions.explanation: Fine-tuning adapts a foundation model's weights using additional domain-specific or task-specific labeled training data. This can improve the model's performance on particular tasks, teach it a specific style or format, or specialize it for a domain. It does not change the context window size, compress parameters, or enable internet access.

questions.question: Which technique is most appropriate when you want to change the behavior of a foundation model WITHOUT modifying its weights?

options.A: Fine-tuning
options.B: Continued pre-training
options.C: Prompt engineering
options.D: Transfer learning with full retraining

questions.explanation: Prompt engineering involves crafting effective prompts (including system prompts, few-shot examples, and instructions) to guide the model's behavior without modifying its weights. Fine-tuning, continued pre-training, and transfer learning all involve updating the model's weights. Prompt engineering is the fastest and most cost-effective way to customize model behavior.

questions.question: A financial services company needs to ensure that their generative AI chatbot never provides specific investment advice. Which Bedrock Guardrails capability is most appropriate?

options.A: Content category filters for financial topics
options.B: Denied topic filters configured for investment advice
options.C: PII redaction filters
options.D: Word filters blocking financial terminology

questions.explanation: Denied topic filters allow you to define specific topics (like providing investment advice) that the model must refuse to engage with. This is more precise than blocking all financial terminology (which would prevent legitimate discussions) or content category filters (which target harmful content categories, not business-specific topics). PII redaction handles personal data, not topic restrictions.

questions.question: What is the context window of a large language model?

options.A: The graphical user interface through which users interact with the model
options.B: The maximum amount of text (measured in tokens) that the model can process in a single request, including both input and output
options.C: The time window during which the model remembers previous conversations
options.D: The number of users that can access the model simultaneously

questions.explanation: The context window is the maximum number of tokens (input prompt plus generated output) that an LLM can process in a single request. It determines how much text the model can consider at once. Models with larger context windows can handle longer documents and conversations. It is not a GUI, a time-based memory, or a concurrency measure.

questions.question: An organization wants to build a generative AI assistant that respects existing document-level access permissions. Employees should only get answers from documents they are authorized to view. Which AWS service supports this natively?

options.A: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
options.B: Amazon Q Business
options.C: Amazon Kendra
options.D: Amazon Comprehend

questions.explanation: Amazon Q Business natively respects existing access control lists (ACLs) and permissions from connected data sources. When an employee asks a question, Q Business only retrieves and uses documents that the employee is authorized to access, based on the permissions configured in the source systems (SharePoint, Confluence, etc.). While Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports metadata filtering, Q Business provides the most seamless enterprise access control integration.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a generative AI application pattern for text summarization?

options.A: Classifying customer emails as positive or negative sentiment
options.B: Condensing a 50-page research report into a 2-paragraph executive summary
options.C: Translating a document from English to French
options.D: Detecting named entities in a news article

questions.explanation: Text summarization involves condensing a long document into a shorter version while preserving the key information and meaning. Condensing a 50-page report into a 2-paragraph summary is a classic summarization task. Sentiment classification, translation, and entity detection are different NLP tasks (classification, translation, and NER respectively).

questions.question: What is the primary function of Cohere's models available on Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: Image generation and editing
options.B: Text generation, embeddings, and reranking for search and RAG
options.C: Video transcription and captioning
options.D: Speech synthesis and voice cloning

questions.explanation: Cohere offers text generation models (Command, Command R, Command R+) and embedding models (Embed) on Amazon Bedrock. Cohere's models are particularly strong in enterprise search, RAG, and multilingual text tasks. They also provide a Rerank model for improving search result relevance. Cohere does not offer image generation, video transcription, or speech synthesis models.

questions.question: A developer needs to build a Bedrock Agent that can check inventory levels by calling a REST API. What must the developer provide to define this capability?

options.A: A fine-tuned model specifically for inventory management
options.B: An action group with a Lambda function or OpenAPI schema describing the API
options.C: A Knowledge Base populated with inventory data
options.D: A Guardrail configured for inventory-related topics

questions.explanation: To enable a Bedrock Agent to call an external REST API, the developer must define an action group. The action group is backed by either an AWS Lambda function that executes the API call or an OpenAPI schema that describes the API endpoints, parameters, and responses. The agent then uses this definition to determine when and how to call the API during task orchestration.

questions.question: What type of learning is primarily used to pre-train foundation models?

options.A: Supervised learning with labeled datasets
options.B: Self-supervised learning on large, unlabeled datasets
options.C: Reinforcement learning from human feedback only
options.D: Active learning with human-in-the-loop annotation

questions.explanation: Foundation models are primarily pre-trained using self-supervised learning on large, unlabeled datasets. The model learns to predict missing or next tokens in text (or masked patches in images) without requiring explicit human labels. This enables training on massive internet-scale corpora. RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) is typically applied after pre-training as a fine-tuning step, not the primary pre-training method.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Amazon Bedrock Guardrails is correct?

options.A: Guardrails can only be applied to Amazon Titan models
options.B: Guardrails operate only on model outputs, not on user inputs
options.C: Guardrails can be applied to any model on Bedrock and operate on both inputs and outputs
options.D: Guardrails replace the need for a foundation model entirely

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails are model-agnostic and can be applied to any foundation model available on Bedrock. They evaluate both user inputs (prompts) and model outputs (responses) to enforce content policies, block denied topics, redact PII, and filter harmful content. They do not replace foundation models; they complement them by adding safety layers.

questions.question: What is an approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) algorithm used for in the context of vector databases?

options.A: Training neural networks to generate embeddings
options.B: Efficiently searching for vectors that are most similar to a query vector in high-dimensional space
options.C: Compressing vectors to reduce storage costs
options.D: Converting text documents into vector embeddings

questions.explanation: ANN algorithms are used by vector databases to efficiently find the vectors most similar to a query vector without performing an exhaustive comparison against every vector in the database. This trades a small amount of accuracy for dramatic speed improvements, enabling real-time similarity search over millions or billions of vectors. ANN does not generate or compress embeddings.

questions.question: A company is building a customer support application and wants the foundation model to always respond in a professional tone, include a disclaimer, and follow specific formatting rules. What is the best approach?

options.A: Fine-tune the model on professional customer support transcripts
options.B: Use a system prompt to define the persona, tone, formatting rules, and disclaimer requirements
options.C: Set the temperature to 0
options.D: Use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to enforce tone

questions.explanation: A system prompt (supported by the Converse API and most models) is the most direct and flexible way to define the model's persona, tone, formatting rules, and required elements like disclaimers. It provides instructions that apply to every interaction. Fine-tuning could help but is more expensive and less flexible. Temperature 0 affects randomness, not tone. Guardrails handle safety, not stylistic requirements.

questions.question: Mistral models on Amazon Bedrock are known for which characteristic?

options.A: They are exclusively designed for image generation tasks
options.B: They offer high performance with efficient architectures, including mixture-of-experts models
options.C: They only support French language inputs
options.D: They are the only models that support fine-tuning on Bedrock

questions.explanation: Mistral models (including Mistral 7B, Mixtral 8x7B, Mistral Large) are known for offering strong performance relative to their size, with efficient architectures. The Mixtral models use a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture that activates only a subset of parameters per token, improving efficiency. They support multiple languages and are not limited to French or image generation.

questions.question: In a RAG pipeline, what happens at query time when a user asks a question?

options.A: The question is directly sent to the foundation model without any context
options.B: The question is embedded, similar documents are retrieved from the vector store, and the retrieved context is included in the prompt to the FM
options.C: The foundation model searches the internet for relevant answers
options.D: The question is stored in the vector database for future training

questions.explanation: At query time in a RAG pipeline: (1) the user's question is converted to a vector embedding, (2) the embedding is used to perform a similarity search in the vector database to retrieve the most relevant document chunks, (3) the retrieved chunks are included as context in the prompt sent to the foundation model, and (4) the FM generates an answer grounded in the retrieved context. The FM does not search the internet.

questions.question: Which Amazon service is an AI-powered coding assistant that was formerly known as Amazon CodeWhisperer?

options.A: Amazon Q Business
options.B: Amazon Q Developer
options.C: Amazon CodeGuru
options.D: Amazon Bedrock Agents

questions.explanation: Amazon Q Developer, formerly known as Amazon CodeWhisperer, is an AI-powered coding assistant that provides real-time code suggestions, code transformation, vulnerability scanning, and chat-based assistance within IDEs and the AWS Console. Amazon Q Business is the enterprise knowledge assistant, CodeGuru is a separate code review service, and Bedrock Agents are for task orchestration.

questions.question: What is the key difference between the InvokeModel API and the Converse API in Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: InvokeModel supports streaming while Converse does not
options.B: InvokeModel requires model-specific request formats while Converse provides a unified format across models
options.C: Converse is only available for Amazon Titan models
options.D: InvokeModel is free while Converse has additional charges

questions.explanation: The key difference is that InvokeModel requires developers to format requests and parse responses according to each model's specific schema, while the Converse API provides a unified, model-agnostic format that works across all supported models. Both APIs support streaming. The Converse API is available for multiple model providers, not just Titan. Pricing is based on token usage, not the API choice.

questions.question: A marketing team wants to generate product description variations using generative AI. They want the output to be highly creative and diverse. How should they configure the inference parameters?

options.A: Set temperature to 0 and top-p to 0.1
options.B: Set temperature to a higher value (e.g., 0.8-1.0) and top-p to a higher value (e.g., 0.9)
options.C: Set max tokens to 10 and temperature to 0.5
options.D: Set temperature to 0 and increase the context window

questions.explanation: Higher temperature and top-p values increase the randomness and creativity of the model's output by considering a broader range of tokens during generation. Temperature 0 and low top-p produce deterministic, repetitive outputs. Setting max tokens to 10 would truncate the output. The context window is a model-level characteristic, not a per-request parameter.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the chunking process in Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases?

options.A: Compressing documents to reduce storage costs in S3
options.B: Breaking documents into smaller segments that can be independently embedded and retrieved
options.C: Encrypting document segments for secure storage
options.D: Converting documents from one format to another

questions.explanation: Chunking is the process of splitting documents into smaller, manageable segments that can be independently converted to vector embeddings and stored in the vector database. At retrieval time, the most relevant chunks (not entire documents) are returned. This improves retrieval precision and fits within the model's context window. Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports fixed-size chunking, semantic chunking, and other strategies.

questions.question: A company wants to use generative AI to automatically generate code for their development team. Which generative AI application pattern does this represent?

options.A: Text summarization
options.B: Image generation
options.C: Code generation
options.D: Sentiment analysis

questions.explanation: Code generation is a generative AI application pattern where the model produces source code based on natural language descriptions, comments, or partial code. This pattern is used by tools like Amazon Q Developer to help developers write code faster. Text summarization condenses text, image generation creates images, and sentiment analysis classifies emotional tone.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of using Amazon Bedrock over self-hosting open-source foundation models on Amazon EC2?

options.A: Bedrock provides access to proprietary models that are not available open-source
options.B: Bedrock eliminates the need to manage infrastructure, GPUs, model serving, and scaling
options.C: Bedrock is always cheaper than EC2 for all workloads
options.D: Bedrock supports only Amazon Titan models

questions.explanation: The primary benefit of Amazon Bedrock is that it is fully managed: AWS handles all infrastructure, GPU provisioning, model serving, scaling, and maintenance. Self-hosting on EC2 requires managing instances, GPU drivers, model deployment, load balancing, and scaling. While Bedrock does offer proprietary models, the main advantage is operational simplicity. Bedrock supports models from multiple providers, not just Titan.

questions.question: In the transformer architecture, what is the purpose of positional encoding?

options.A: To identify the language of the input text
options.B: To provide the model with information about the position of each token in the sequence
options.C: To reduce the dimensionality of the input embeddings
options.D: To encrypt the position of sensitive tokens

questions.explanation: Positional encoding (or positional embeddings) provides the transformer model with information about the position and order of tokens in a sequence. Since the self-attention mechanism processes all tokens in parallel (unlike RNNs), it has no inherent notion of token order. Positional encodings are added to the input embeddings to give the model this sequential information.

questions.question: An e-commerce company has product documentation in S3 and wants to build a chatbot that answers product questions. The documents are updated weekly. Which architecture is most appropriate?

options.A: Fine-tune a new model every week with the updated documents
options.B: Use Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with a sync schedule to keep the vector store updated
options.C: Copy all documents into the model's system prompt for each query
options.D: Train a custom model from scratch using the documents

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with a data sync schedule is the ideal approach. The Knowledge Base can be configured to periodically re-ingest documents from S3, updating the vector store with new or changed content. This ensures the chatbot always has access to the latest product information without retraining. Fine-tuning weekly is expensive and slow, copying all docs exceeds context limits, and training from scratch is impractical.

questions.question: What is the Converse API's tool use (function calling) capability in Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: The ability to call AWS CLI commands from within the model
options.B: The ability for the model to request that the application execute a specific function, then incorporate the result into its response
options.C: The ability to install third-party plugins into the model
options.D: The ability to use multiple models simultaneously for a single query

questions.explanation: Tool use (function calling) in the Converse API allows the model to indicate that it needs to call a specific function to complete a task. The application defines available tools with their schemas. When the model determines it needs external data or actions, it returns a tool use request. The application executes the function and returns the result, which the model incorporates into its final response. This enables models to interact with external systems.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings?

options.A: A model that generates both text and images simultaneously
options.B: A model that converts both text and image inputs into a shared vector embedding space
options.C: A model that translates text in images to different languages
options.D: A model that creates 3D models from 2D images

questions.explanation: Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings converts both text and image inputs into vectors in a shared embedding space. This means text descriptions and images of similar concepts will have vectors that are close together, enabling cross-modal search (finding images by text description or finding text by similar images). It does not generate content or translate text in images.

questions.question: A company using Amazon Bedrock wants to prevent the model from generating responses that contain hallucinated facts not supported by the provided context. Which Guardrails feature addresses this?

options.A: Denied topic filters
options.B: Word filters
options.C: Automated reasoning checks (contextual grounding checks)
options.D: PII redaction filters

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails includes automated reasoning checks (also called contextual grounding checks) that evaluate whether the model's response is factually grounded in the provided source material or context. If the response contains claims not supported by the context, the guardrail can block or flag the response, helping to mitigate hallucinations.

questions.question: What is few-shot prompting?

options.A: Training a model with a small dataset of a few hundred examples
options.B: Including a few input-output examples in the prompt to guide the model's behavior without modifying its weights
options.C: Running the model inference multiple times and selecting the best output
options.D: Reducing the number of parameters in a model for faster inference

questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting is a prompt engineering technique where you include a small number of input-output examples in the prompt to demonstrate the desired behavior, format, or task to the model. The model uses these examples as in-context learning to produce appropriate responses. No model weights are modified. Zero-shot prompting uses no examples, and one-shot uses a single example.

questions.question: Which AWS service would you use to build a generative AI application that can access and reason over enterprise data from Salesforce, Jira, and Gmail, while respecting individual user access permissions?

options.A: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
options.B: Amazon Q Business
options.C: Amazon Kendra
options.D: Amazon Comprehend

questions.explanation: Amazon Q Business is specifically designed for enterprise use cases, with pre-built connectors for services like Salesforce, Jira, Gmail, SharePoint, Confluence, and more. It natively respects user-level access controls from these systems, ensuring employees only receive answers based on documents they are authorized to access. While Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports RAG, it requires more custom integration for enterprise connectors and access control.

questions.question: What is the difference between continued pre-training and fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: There is no difference; they are the same process
options.B: Continued pre-training uses unlabeled domain data to teach the model domain knowledge, while fine-tuning uses labeled examples to improve task performance
options.C: Continued pre-training is cheaper than fine-tuning
options.D: Fine-tuning uses more data than continued pre-training

questions.explanation: Continued pre-training exposes the model to additional unlabeled domain-specific data (e.g., medical literature, legal documents) to teach it domain-specific knowledge and vocabulary. Fine-tuning uses labeled input-output pairs to teach the model to perform a specific task in a desired format. Both modify model weights, but they serve different purposes and use different types of training data.

questions.question: A developer is building a conversational application and needs to maintain conversation history across multiple turns. Which Amazon Bedrock API feature facilitates this?

options.A: InvokeModel with session IDs
options.B: The Converse API's messages array for managing conversation history
options.C: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases memory feature
options.D: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails conversation tracking

questions.explanation: The Converse API includes a messages array where the application passes the full conversation history (alternating user and assistant messages) with each request. This enables the model to understand the context of the conversation across multiple turns. The application is responsible for maintaining and sending this history. InvokeModel does not have native session management.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid reason to choose Anthropic's Claude models on Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: Claude is the only model that supports image generation on Bedrock
options.B: Claude models offer strong performance in reasoning, analysis, coding, and support very large context windows
options.C: Claude is the only model available on Bedrock
options.D: Claude models are exclusively designed for healthcare applications

questions.explanation: Anthropic's Claude models are known for their strong reasoning, analysis, and coding capabilities, and they support very large context windows (up to 200K tokens for some versions). Claude is not the only model on Bedrock (many providers are available), does not generate images (that's Stable Diffusion and Titan Image Generator), and is a general-purpose model not limited to healthcare.

questions.question: In the context of generative AI, what is a hallucination?

options.A: When the model generates a realistic image that looks like a photograph
options.B: When the model generates plausible-sounding but factually incorrect or fabricated information
options.C: When the model produces output in a language different from the input
options.D: When the model fails to generate any output at all

questions.explanation: A hallucination in generative AI occurs when the model generates information that sounds plausible and confident but is factually incorrect, fabricated, or not supported by the source data. This is one of the key challenges with LLMs. Techniques like RAG, guardrails with grounding checks, and careful prompt engineering help mitigate hallucinations.

questions.question: What is the maximum benefit of using Amazon Bedrock Agents compared to using the foundation model alone?

options.A: Agents generate higher quality text than the base model
options.B: Agents can autonomously take actions, call external APIs, and complete multi-step tasks
options.C: Agents are cheaper to operate than direct model invocations
options.D: Agents do not require a foundation model to operate

questions.explanation: The primary benefit of Bedrock Agents is their ability to autonomously decompose complex requests into multiple steps, call external APIs through action groups, query knowledge bases, and orchestrate multi-step workflows. A foundation model alone can only generate text; it cannot take real-world actions. Agents still require a foundation model as their reasoning engine.

questions.question: Which of the following vector databases can be used with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases? (Select the best answer)

options.A: Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon Neptune
options.B: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Pinecone, and Redis Enterprise Cloud
options.C: Only Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
options.D: MongoDB Atlas and Cassandra

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports several vector store options: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (vector engine), Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (with pgvector extension), Pinecone, and Redis Enterprise Cloud. It also supports Amazon Neptune Analytics for graph-based retrieval. DynamoDB, Neptune (standard), MongoDB, and Cassandra are not supported vector stores for Bedrock Knowledge Bases.

questions.question: An application needs to generate embeddings for 10 million product descriptions to enable semantic search. Which Amazon Bedrock model should be used?

options.A: Anthropic Claude 3 Sonnet
options.B: Amazon Titan Embeddings G1
options.C: Stability AI Stable Diffusion XL
options.D: Meta Llama 3

questions.explanation: Amazon Titan Embeddings G1 is specifically designed to convert text into vector embeddings for semantic search, similarity matching, and RAG pipelines. Claude, Llama, and Stable Diffusion are generative models designed for text generation or image generation, not for producing vector embeddings for search.

questions.question: What is the relationship between Amazon Bedrock and PartyRock?

options.A: PartyRock is a premium tier of Amazon Bedrock for enterprise customers
options.B: PartyRock is powered by Amazon Bedrock and provides a no-code interface for building generative AI apps
options.C: PartyRock is a competitor to Amazon Bedrock from a different company
options.D: PartyRock replaces Amazon Bedrock for all consumer applications

questions.explanation: PartyRock is powered by Amazon Bedrock's foundation models and provides a no-code, browser-based interface for building generative AI applications. It serves as an accessible entry point for learning about and experimenting with generative AI without needing an AWS account or coding skills. It complements, rather than replaces, Amazon Bedrock.

questions.question: A company wants to use a diffusion model for generating marketing images. Which concept describes how diffusion models generate images?

options.A: The model retrieves and combines existing images from a database
options.B: The model iteratively removes noise from a random noise pattern, guided by the text prompt, to produce a coherent image
options.C: The model renders 3D scenes from text descriptions using ray tracing
options.D: The model searches the internet for the most relevant existing image

questions.explanation: Diffusion models work by starting with random noise and iteratively denoising it over many steps, guided by the conditioning signal (typically a text prompt encoded by a text encoder). Through this denoising process, a coherent image that matches the prompt gradually emerges. This is how Stable Diffusion and Titan Image Generator produce images. They do not retrieve, combine, or search for existing images.

questions.question: When using Amazon Bedrock, how is pricing typically calculated for foundation model inference?

options.A: A flat monthly fee regardless of usage
options.B: Based on the number of input and output tokens processed
options.C: Based on the number of API calls regardless of content size
options.D: Based on the time the model spends processing each request

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock on-demand pricing is based on the number of input tokens (in the prompt) and output tokens (in the response) processed by the model. Different models have different per-token prices, and input tokens are typically cheaper than output tokens. For image models, pricing is per image generated. Provisioned throughput uses a time-based pricing model for reserved capacity.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a capability of Amazon Q Developer?

options.A: Real-time code suggestions in the IDE
options.B: Code transformation (e.g., Java 8 to Java 17 upgrade)
options.C: Training custom foundation models from scratch
options.D: Security vulnerability scanning in code

questions.explanation: Amazon Q Developer provides code suggestions, code transformation (language version upgrades), security vulnerability scanning, chat-based debugging, and AWS resource management assistance. It does not train custom foundation models from scratch. That capability is provided by services like Amazon SageMaker or Amazon Bedrock's custom model training features.

questions.question: A retail company wants to build an AI assistant that can check order status, process returns, and recommend products in a single conversation. The assistant needs to call different backend APIs depending on the user's request. Which architecture should they use?

options.A: Amazon Bedrock with InvokeModel API and manual API calls in application code
options.B: Amazon Bedrock Agent with action groups for each backend API
options.C: Amazon Lex with Lambda integrations
options.D: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with all order data

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Agents with action groups is the best architecture for this use case. Each backend API (order status, returns, recommendations) can be defined as an action group backed by Lambda functions. The agent autonomously decides which APIs to call based on the conversation, handles multi-step workflows, and synthesizes responses. This is more flexible than manually orchestrating API calls or using Lex for complex multi-API interactions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the stop sequences parameter in LLM inference?

options.A: To define words that should be censored in the output
options.B: To specify character sequences that signal the model to stop generating further tokens
options.C: To set the maximum runtime for model inference
options.D: To configure the model to stop accepting new requests

questions.explanation: Stop sequences are character strings that, when generated by the model, signal it to stop producing further tokens. This is useful for controlling output format, preventing the model from generating beyond a desired endpoint (e.g., stopping after a specific delimiter), and ensuring clean output boundaries. They are different from content filters or runtime limits.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and data sources is correct?

options.A: Knowledge Bases can only ingest data from Amazon S3
options.B: Knowledge Bases support data from Amazon S3, web crawlers, Confluence, Salesforce, SharePoint, and custom data sources
options.C: Knowledge Bases require all data to be in JSON format
options.D: Knowledge Bases can only ingest data in real-time streams

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports multiple data source types including Amazon S3 (the most common), web crawlers, Confluence, Salesforce, SharePoint, and custom data sources via the custom connector. Documents can be in various formats including PDF, TXT, HTML, Markdown, DOC/DOCX, and CSV. Data is ingested through batch sync jobs, not real-time streams.

questions.question: A developer is using Amazon Bedrock and wants to ensure predictable, consistent outputs for a classification task. How should they configure the inference parameters?

options.A: Set temperature to 1.0 and top-p to 1.0
options.B: Set temperature to 0 (or near 0) for deterministic output
options.C: Set max tokens to the maximum value
options.D: Use a larger model with more parameters

questions.explanation: For classification tasks where consistent, predictable outputs are needed, setting the temperature to 0 (or very close to 0) makes the model deterministic. It will always select the most probable token at each step, producing the same output for the same input. High temperature introduces randomness. Max tokens and model size don't directly affect output consistency.

questions.question: What is chain-of-thought reasoning in the context of Amazon Bedrock Agents?

options.A: A blockchain-based verification system for agent actions
options.B: The agent's process of decomposing a complex request into logical steps and reasoning about which actions to take
options.C: A method of chaining multiple models together in a pipeline
options.D: A logging mechanism that records every API call in sequence

questions.explanation: Chain-of-thought reasoning in Bedrock Agents refers to the agent's ability to break down a complex user request into logical steps, reason about which actions need to be taken, in what order, and with what parameters. The agent generates an internal reasoning trace that shows its thought process as it orchestrates calls to action groups and knowledge bases to fulfill the request.

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of using the Converse API's tool use feature over implementing external API calls manually in application code?

options.A: Tool use is faster than direct API calls
options.B: The model decides when and how to use tools based on the conversation context, making the interaction more natural and intelligent
options.C: Tool use eliminates the need for any backend services
options.D: Tool use provides built-in error handling for all external APIs

questions.explanation: The key benefit of tool use is that the foundation model itself decides when a tool needs to be called based on the conversation context, what parameters to pass, and how to incorporate the results into its response. This makes interactions more natural and intelligent compared to hard-coded API call logic. The application still needs to execute the actual API calls and provide backend services.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate their application from using Claude to using Llama on Amazon Bedrock. They are currently using the InvokeModel API with Claude-specific prompt formatting. What is the most efficient migration path?

options.A: Rewrite the application to use Llama-specific prompt formatting with InvokeModel
options.B: Refactor the application to use the Converse API, which provides a model-agnostic interface
options.C: Use Amazon Bedrock Agents to abstract away the model differences
options.D: Fine-tune Llama to accept Claude-formatted prompts

questions.explanation: Migrating to the Converse API is the most efficient approach because it provides a unified, model-agnostic interface. Once migrated, the application can switch between any supported model (Claude, Llama, Titan, etc.) by simply changing the model ID, without reformatting prompts. Rewriting for Llama-specific formatting works but would need to be redone for every future model switch.

questions.question: What is the role of the embedding model in a RAG architecture?

options.A: To generate the final answer to the user's question
options.B: To convert both documents and queries into vector representations that enable semantic similarity search
options.C: To translate documents into the user's preferred language
options.D: To classify documents into predefined categories

questions.explanation: In a RAG architecture, the embedding model serves two purposes: (1) during ingestion, it converts document chunks into vector representations stored in the vector database, and (2) at query time, it converts the user's question into a vector in the same embedding space. This enables semantic similarity search to find the most relevant document chunks for the query. A separate generative model produces the final answer.

questions.question: Which AWS service allows business users to create generative AI applications by connecting to corporate knowledge sources without requiring ML expertise?

options.A: Amazon SageMaker
options.B: Amazon Q Business
options.C: Amazon Bedrock
options.D: AWS Glue

questions.explanation: Amazon Q Business is designed for business users to create generative AI-powered assistants that connect to corporate knowledge sources through pre-built connectors. It requires no ML expertise and handles data ingestion, indexing, and response generation automatically. SageMaker and Bedrock require more technical expertise, and AWS Glue is an ETL service.

questions.question: What is the purpose of multi-head attention in the transformer architecture?

options.A: To process multiple documents simultaneously
options.B: To allow the model to attend to different representation subspaces and capture different types of relationships between tokens
options.C: To enable the model to generate multiple outputs in parallel
options.D: To split the model across multiple GPUs for distributed training

questions.explanation: Multi-head attention allows the transformer to compute attention in multiple parallel representation subspaces (heads). Each head can learn to attend to different types of relationships (e.g., syntactic dependencies, semantic relationships, positional patterns). The outputs of all heads are concatenated and linearly transformed. This gives the model a richer representation than single-head attention.

questions.question: A company needs to generate embeddings for both product images and product descriptions so that customers can search for products using either text or image queries. Which Amazon model should they use?

options.A: Amazon Titan Text Embeddings
options.B: Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings
options.C: Amazon Titan Image Generator
options.D: Anthropic Claude with vision capabilities

questions.explanation: Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings can process both text and image inputs and map them into a shared vector embedding space. This enables cross-modal search: customers can search using text to find relevant product images, or use an image to find products with similar descriptions. Titan Text Embeddings only handles text, Titan Image Generator creates images, and Claude with vision understands images but doesn't produce search embeddings.

questions.question: What does the max_tokens (or maxTokens) parameter control in a Bedrock model invocation?

options.A: The maximum size of the input prompt
options.B: The maximum number of tokens the model will generate in its response
options.C: The maximum number of API calls allowed per minute
options.D: The maximum number of models that can be invoked in parallel

questions.explanation: The max_tokens parameter sets an upper limit on the number of tokens the model will generate in its response. Once this limit is reached, generation stops even if the response is incomplete. It does not affect the input size (which is limited by the context window), API rate limits, or model parallelism.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios is best addressed by Amazon Bedrock Guardrails' content category filters?

options.A: Preventing the model from discussing competitor products
options.B: Blocking responses that contain hate speech, violence, sexual content, or misconduct
options.C: Masking Social Security numbers in user inputs
options.D: Limiting the model's response length

questions.explanation: Content category filters in Bedrock Guardrails detect and block content across predefined harmful categories including hate speech, insults, sexual content, violence, and misconduct. Each category can be configured with adjustable strength levels. Blocking competitor topics uses denied topic filters, masking SSNs uses PII filters, and response length is controlled by the max_tokens parameter.

questions.question: A developer wants to use Amazon Bedrock to build an application that can analyze uploaded images and answer questions about them. Which type of foundation model should they choose?

options.A: A text-only LLM like Cohere Command
options.B: A multimodal model like Anthropic Claude 3 that supports both text and image inputs
options.C: An embedding model like Titan Embeddings
options.D: An image generation model like Stable Diffusion

questions.explanation: For analyzing uploaded images and answering questions about them (visual question answering), a multimodal model that accepts both text and image inputs is needed. Anthropic's Claude 3 family supports vision capabilities, allowing it to analyze images and respond to text questions about them. Text-only models cannot process images, embedding models produce vectors rather than answers, and Stable Diffusion generates images rather than analyzing them.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the system prompt in the Converse API?

options.A: To configure the model's inference parameters like temperature and top-p
options.B: To provide persistent instructions that define the model's persona, behavior rules, and context for the entire conversation
options.C: To authenticate the API request
options.D: To specify which foundation model to use

questions.explanation: The system prompt in the Converse API provides instructions that apply to the entire conversation. It typically defines the model's persona, behavior guidelines, tone, formatting rules, and relevant context. Unlike user messages, the system prompt persists across all turns and is not part of the visible conversation. Inference parameters, authentication, and model selection are handled through other API fields.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between tokens and words in LLMs?

options.A: One token always equals one word
options.B: One token always equals one character
options.C: Tokens can represent sub-words, whole words, or characters, and one word may be split into multiple tokens
options.D: Tokens are only used for numbers, not text

questions.explanation: Tokens in LLMs can represent sub-word units, whole words, punctuation, or individual characters, depending on the tokenization scheme (e.g., BPE, SentencePiece). Common words are often a single token, while rare or long words may be split into multiple tokens. As a rough estimate, one token is approximately 3/4 of a word in English, but this varies significantly.

questions.question: A company has deployed a generative AI application on Amazon Bedrock and wants to monitor which Guardrail policies are being triggered most frequently. What should they use?

options.A: Amazon CloudWatch metrics and logs for Bedrock Guardrails
options.B: Amazon Inspector
options.C: AWS Config rules
options.D: Amazon Detective

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails integrates with Amazon CloudWatch, which captures metrics on guardrail invocations, interventions, and the specific policies being triggered. This allows teams to monitor guardrail effectiveness, identify patterns in blocked content, and adjust configurations as needed. Inspector is for vulnerability scanning, Config is for resource compliance, and Detective is for security investigation.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between Amazon Q Business and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases?

options.A: Q Business uses vector databases while Knowledge Bases does not
options.B: Q Business is a complete enterprise assistant solution with built-in connectors and access controls, while Knowledge Bases is a RAG building block within Bedrock for developers
options.C: Knowledge Bases supports more data formats than Q Business
options.D: Q Business only works with Amazon Titan models

questions.explanation: Amazon Q Business is a fully managed, end-to-end enterprise assistant solution that includes pre-built data source connectors, native access control integration, a web interface, and admin controls. Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases is a developer-focused RAG building block that provides more flexibility and customization but requires developers to build the application layer. Q Business is higher-level; Knowledge Bases is a lower-level component.

questions.question: In which scenario would continued pre-training be preferred over fine-tuning on Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: When you need the model to follow a specific input-output format for classification
options.B: When you want to expose the model to a large corpus of domain-specific language and terminology (e.g., medical, legal, or financial jargon)
options.C: When you need the model to generate images in a specific style
options.D: When you want to reduce the model's response latency

questions.explanation: Continued pre-training is ideal when you want the model to absorb domain-specific knowledge, terminology, and language patterns from a large unlabeled corpus (e.g., medical journals, legal documents, financial reports). This extends the model's foundational knowledge. Fine-tuning is better for teaching the model specific task behaviors using labeled examples. Neither approach reduces latency or enables image style transfer.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about how Amazon Bedrock Agents handle knowledge base queries?

options.A: Agents cannot access Knowledge Bases; they only call external APIs
options.B: Agents can be configured to query one or more Knowledge Bases as part of their task orchestration
options.C: Agents replace Knowledge Bases entirely
options.D: Agents require a separate Bedrock account to access Knowledge Bases

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Agents can be configured to query one or more Knowledge Bases as part of their task orchestration, in addition to calling external APIs through action groups. This allows an agent to combine data retrieval from knowledge bases with API actions. For example, an agent could look up product information from a Knowledge Base and then check inventory via an API.
