questions.question: A company wants to build a generative AI application that summarizes customer support tickets and assigns them priority levels. Which combination of generative AI patterns is involved?

options.A: Image generation and translation
options.B: Summarization and classification
options.C: Code generation and question answering
options.D: Embeddings and image analysis

questions.explanation: This application involves two generative AI patterns: summarization (condensing support tickets into shorter summaries) and classification (assigning priority levels such as high, medium, low). Both tasks can be performed by a single LLM with appropriate prompting. Image generation, translation, code generation, and image analysis are not relevant to this use case.

questions.question: What is Amazon Bedrock model evaluation used for?

options.A: To evaluate the cost of running different models
options.B: To compare the quality of different foundation models on specific tasks using automatic metrics or human evaluation
options.C: To evaluate the security posture of the Bedrock service
options.D: To evaluate whether a model needs fine-tuning

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation allows users to assess and compare foundation model performance on specific tasks. It supports automatic evaluation using built-in metrics (accuracy, robustness, toxicity) with benchmark datasets, as well as human evaluation using custom workforces. This helps teams select the best model for their use case. It does not evaluate costs or security posture.

questions.question: Which of the following accurately describes the concept of transfer learning as it relates to foundation models?

options.A: Moving a trained model from one AWS Region to another
options.B: Leveraging a model's pre-trained knowledge on a broad dataset and applying it to new, specific tasks with minimal additional training
options.C: Transferring data between databases for model training
options.D: Copying model weights between different cloud providers

questions.explanation: Transfer learning is the concept of taking a model that has been pre-trained on a large, diverse dataset and adapting it to new, specific tasks with relatively little additional training. Foundation models are a prime example: pre-trained on broad internet data, they can be fine-tuned or prompt-engineered for specific use cases. This is far more efficient than training a model from scratch for each task.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application and notices that the retrieved chunks sometimes lack sufficient context because they are too small. What should they adjust?

options.A: Increase the model's temperature parameter
options.B: Adjust the chunk size and overlap settings in the Knowledge Base configuration
options.C: Switch to a different foundation model
options.D: Add more Guardrails to the application

questions.explanation: If retrieved chunks lack sufficient context, the developer should increase the chunk size in the Knowledge Base ingestion configuration. They can also configure chunk overlap to ensure context is not lost at chunk boundaries. Larger chunks provide more context per retrieval result. Temperature affects output randomness, model switching doesn't fix chunking, and Guardrails handle content safety, not retrieval quality.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of using Amazon Bedrock over building a generative AI solution using only open-source models on EC2?

options.A: Bedrock offers access to both proprietary and open-source models through a single API with no infrastructure management
options.B: Bedrock is the only way to use open-source models on AWS
options.C: Bedrock always provides lower latency than EC2-hosted models
options.D: Bedrock guarantees 100% accuracy from all models

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock provides access to both proprietary models (Claude, Titan) and open-source models (Llama, Mistral) through a single, unified API with no infrastructure to manage. This is a key advantage over self-hosting on EC2, where you must manage instances, GPUs, model serving, and scaling. Open-source models can also be hosted on SageMaker or EC2 (so Bedrock isn't the only way), and no service guarantees 100% model accuracy.

questions.question: What is semantic search, and how does it differ from keyword search?

options.A: Semantic search is slower than keyword search and produces worse results
options.B: Semantic search uses vector embeddings to match by meaning rather than exact keywords, finding relevant results even when different words are used
options.C: Semantic search requires a SQL database while keyword search requires NoSQL
options.D: There is no difference; both produce identical results

questions.explanation: Semantic search uses vector embeddings to understand the meaning of queries and documents, finding relevant results based on conceptual similarity even when exact keywords don't match. For example, a search for 'automobile' would find documents about 'cars' and 'vehicles.' Keyword search relies on exact or partial text matches and would miss semantically related terms. Semantic search is fundamental to RAG pipelines.

questions.question: A company wants to deploy a generative AI application that handles both English and Spanish customer queries. Which factor should they consider when selecting a foundation model on Bedrock?

options.A: The model's context window size only
options.B: The model's multilingual capabilities and performance in both English and Spanish
options.C: The model's image generation quality
options.D: The model's ability to generate code

questions.explanation: When building a multilingual application, the most important factor is selecting a model with strong capabilities in the required languages. Models like Claude, Llama, and Cohere Command R+ have strong multilingual performance. The company should evaluate each model's performance in both English and Spanish through model evaluation or testing. Context window, image generation, and code generation are less relevant to this requirement.

questions.question: What is inpainting in the context of Amazon Titan Image Generator?

options.A: Generating a completely new image from a text prompt
options.B: Modifying or replacing specific areas within an existing image based on a text prompt and a mask
options.C: Converting a color image to black and white
options.D: Adding a text watermark to an image

questions.explanation: Inpainting is the process of modifying or replacing specific areas within an existing image. The user provides the original image, a mask that indicates which area to change, and a text prompt describing the desired change. Titan Image Generator then regenerates only the masked area based on the prompt while preserving the rest of the image. This is different from text-to-image generation (creating from scratch) or outpainting (extending borders).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture used in models like Mixtral on Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: A model that combines outputs from multiple completely separate models
options.B: An architecture where only a subset of the model's parameters (experts) are activated for each token, improving efficiency while maintaining a large total parameter count
options.C: A model that requires multiple human experts to verify its outputs
options.D: An architecture that runs the same model on multiple GPUs simultaneously

questions.explanation: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) is an architecture where the model contains multiple 'expert' sub-networks, but only a subset of them are activated for each input token via a learned routing mechanism. This allows the model to have a very large total number of parameters (and thus capacity) while keeping inference cost lower, since only a fraction of parameters are used per token. Mixtral 8x7B, for example, has 8 experts but activates only 2 per token.

questions.question: A company is building a customer-facing generative AI chatbot and wants to implement multiple safety layers. Which combination of Amazon Bedrock features provides the most comprehensive safety approach?

options.A: Knowledge Bases and Agents only
options.B: Guardrails with content filters, denied topics, PII redaction, and grounding checks, combined with a well-crafted system prompt
options.C: Provisioned throughput and model evaluation
options.D: Fine-tuning and continued pre-training

questions.explanation: The most comprehensive safety approach combines Bedrock Guardrails (content category filters for harmful content, denied topic filters for off-topic conversations, PII redaction for data privacy, and grounding checks for hallucination prevention) with a well-crafted system prompt that defines appropriate behavior. This creates multiple layers of safety. Knowledge Bases, Agents, provisioned throughput, and model evaluation serve different purposes and do not directly address safety.

questions.question: A startup wants to quickly prototype a generative AI-powered trip planning application to validate their idea before investing in development. They have no AWS account and no developers on the team. What is the fastest path to a working prototype?

options.A: Sign up for an AWS account and use Amazon Bedrock APIs
options.B: Use PartyRock to build a no-code generative AI app for trip planning
options.C: Deploy an open-source model on Amazon EC2
options.D: Use Amazon SageMaker to train a custom trip planning model

questions.explanation: PartyRock is the fastest path because it requires no AWS account, no coding skills, and no infrastructure setup. The startup can describe their trip planning app in natural language and use PartyRock's drag-and-drop widgets to create a working prototype in minutes. This allows them to validate the concept and experiment with prompts before committing to a full development effort with Bedrock or other services.
